9:22: Aharon raised his hands toward the people and he blessed them.

10:4: Moshe called to Mishael and to Elzafan
the sons of Uziel, the brother of the father of Aharon,
and said to them; Come closer and carry your brothers from the presence of the Sanctuary,
10:7: From the entrance of the Tent of Meeting you shall not go forth lest you die;
for the oil of the inauguration to greatness of Adonoy is on you
and they did as Moshe had said.
10:12: Moshe spoke to Aharon and to Elozor and Isomor, his surviving sons;
Take the meal-offering which remains of the offerings of Adonoy
and eat it [as] matzoh [unleavened] beside the altar,
for it is holy of holies [=most holy].
10:13: You shall eat it in a sacred place,
for it is your portion and the portion of your sons
for so have I been commanded.
10:14: The breast of the uplifted-offering and the thigh that is the separated portion you shall eat in a pure (undefiled) place,
you and your sons and daughters with you,
for as your portion and as the portion of your sons they are given
from the sacrifices of the sacred-offerings of Bnei Yisroel.
10:15: The thigh that is the separated portion and the breast that is the uplifted-offering, on top of the fats of the offering, they shall bring,
to lift up as an uplifted-offering before Adonoy.
It will be for you and for your sons with you an everlasting statute,
10:19: Aharon spoke [in reply] to Moshe, Behold, today they brought their sin-offerings and their burnt-offerings before Adonoy
If I had eaten the sin-offering today,
would that have been fitting before Adonoy?
10:20: and it was pleasing in his eyes.
11:3: All that have a cloven hoof, and they [the hooves] are [completely] split
and that [also] brings up dissolved food among animals,
11:4: However, these in particular you may not eat
of those that bring up dissolved food
the camel, for he brings up dissolved food but does not have a split hoof
11:5: The jumping rabbit , for it brings up dissolved food
but does not have a cloven hoof
11:6: The hare, for it brings up dissolved food
but it does not have a cloven hoof
11:7: The pig, for though it has cloven hooves, and its hooves are [completely] split —
it does not bring up dissolved food —
11:14: The falcon and the tearing vulture, to its kind.
11:17: The little owl, the fish drawer and the eagle owl.
11:19: and the heron, to its kind.
11:26: Thus every animal that has cloven hooves but its hooves are not [completely] split and it does not bring up its dissolved food,
all who touch them shall become unclean.
11:36: However, a well-spring and a pit, a place of gathered water, shall be pure.
[But] that which touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
